title: Atomic-resolution Li Analysis in Al-Li Alloy System by Electron Energy-loss Spectrometry in an Aberration-Corrected Scanning Transmission Electron Microscope
content: Characterization of lower atomic number elements, especially below carbon (Z < 6), is very challenging in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) mainly due to lower electron scattering, which results in very limited signals for imaging and more seriously for analysis. Lithium (Li: Z = 3) is one of those light elements hardly characterized in TEM although there are high demands of appropriate characterization especially for development of Li-based battery materials. So far, annular bright-field (ABF) scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging is the most efficient and reliable approach to image Li atoms at atomic-resolution levels. However, Li analysis is still very challenging in electron energy-loss spectrometry (EELS). Recently, we have developed an EELS system based on a CEOS energy-filtering and imaging device (CEFID) [1] to detect higher energy-loss electrons up to 13,000 eV, and installed it into an existing aberration-corrected S/TEM JEOL JEM-ARM200CF at Lehigh. To collect limited EELS signals at higher energy-loss regions, a highly sensitive hybrid-pixel electron detector Dectris ELA was integrated into the CEFID system. In this study, we have applied the CEFID-based EELS system for Li characterization in Al-Li alloy system as a case study.
